111	class SeriesStore:
112	    """Append-mostly time series store persisted under ``root``.
113	
114	    Layout::
115	
116	        <root>/series.json                 registry: series_id -> series row
117	        <root>/points/<series_id>.jsonl    one ``{"t":ts,"v":value}`` per line
118	        <root>/quotas.json                 tenant -> {"max_series", "max_points"}
119	    """
120	
121	    def __init__(self, root):
122	        if not isinstance(root, (str, os.PathLike)) or not str(root):
123	            raise ObsError("root must be a non-empty path")
124	        self.root = os.path.abspath(str(root))
125	        self.points_dir = os.path.join(self.root, "points")
126	        self.series_path = os.path.join(self.root, "series.json")
127	        self.quota_path = os.path.join(self.root, "quotas.json")
128	        self._lock = threading.RLock()
129	        self._series, self._samples, self._writes = {}, {}, 0
130	        self._quotas = {}
131	        os.makedirs(self.points_dir, exist_ok=True)
132	        self._load()
133	        self._load_quotas()
134	
135	    def _points_path(self, sid):
136	        return os.path.join(self.points_dir, sid + ".jsonl")
137	
138	    # ------------------------------------------------------------- persistence
139	    def _load(self):
140	        rows = []
141	        if os.path.exists(self.series_path):
142	            try:
143	                with open(self.series_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
144	                    rows = json.load(handle)
145	            except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
146	                raise ObsError("cannot read series registry: %s" % exc)
147	        for row in rows:
148	            sid = row.get("series_id")
149	            if not sid:
150	                continue
151	            self._series[sid] = {"series_id": sid, "tenant": row.get("tenant"),
152	                                 "metric": row.get("metric"),
153	                                 "labels": [[str(k), str(v)] for k, v in row.get("labels", [])],
154	                                 "identity": row.get("identity")}
155	            self._samples[sid] = self._read_points(sid)
156	
157	    def _read_points(self, sid):
158	        """Reload one point file, skipping unreadable lines.
159	
160	        Repeated lines for the same timestamp (left behind by historical
161	        overwrites) collapse to the last value stored, so occupancy counts each
162	        distinct timestamp once after a reopen.
163	        """
164	        rows = {}
165	        path = self._points_path(sid)
166	        if os.path.exists(path):
167	            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
168	                for line in handle:
169	                    try:
170	                        row = json.loads(line)
171	                        rows[int(row["t"])] = float(row["v"])
172	                    except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
173	                        continue
174	        return sorted(rows.items())
175	
176	    def _save_registry(self):
177	        _atomic_write(self.series_path, json.dumps(
178	            [self._series[sid] for sid in sorted(self._series)],
179	            sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")))
180	
181	    def _rewrite_points(self, sid):
182	        _atomic_write(self._points_path(sid),
183	                      "".join(_line(ts, value) for ts, value in self._samples[sid]))
184	
185	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ quotas
186	    def _load_quotas(self):
187	        """Reload ``quotas.json``; a missing file means every tenant is unlimited."""
188	        if not os.path.exists(self.quota_path):
189	            return
190	        try:
191	            with open(self.quota_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
192	                data = json.load(handle)
193	        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
194	            raise ObsError("cannot read quota config: %s" % exc)
195	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
196	            raise ObsError("cannot read quota config: root must be an object")
197	        for tenant, row in data.items():
198	            if not isinstance(tenant, str) or not tenant or not isinstance(row, dict):
199	                raise ObsError("cannot read quota config: malformed entry")
200	            self._quotas[tenant] = {
201	                "max_series": self._clean_limit(row.get("max_series"), "max_series"),
202	                "max_points": self._clean_limit(row.get("max_points"), "max_points")}
203	
204	    @staticmethod
205	    def _clean_limit(value, field):
206	        """A limit is a non-negative integer or ``None`` (unlimited)."""
207	        if value is None:
208	            return None
209	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
210	            raise ObsError("%s must be a non-negative integer or null" % field)
211	        if value < 0:
212	            raise ObsError("%s must be a non-negative integer or null" % field)
213	        return value
214	
215	    @staticmethod
216	    def _clean_tenant(tenant):
217	        if not isinstance(tenant, str) or not tenant:
218	            raise ObsError("tenant must be a non-empty string")
219	        return tenant
220	
221	    def _save_quotas(self):
222	        _atomic_write(self.quota_path, json.dumps(
223	            {tenant: self._quotas[tenant] for tenant in sorted(self._quotas)},
224	            sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")))
225	
226	    def set_quota(self, tenant, max_series, max_points):
227	        """Configure the per-tenant limits; ``None`` means unlimited.
228	
229	        Limits may be lowered below current usage; pure duplicate/overwrite
230	        writes stay allowed afterwards. Configuring a quota never creates a
231	        series.
232	        """
233	        tenant = self._clean_tenant(tenant)
234	        max_series = self._clean_limit(max_series, "max_series")
235	        max_points = self._clean_limit(max_points, "max_points")
236	        with self._lock:
237	            self._quotas[tenant] = {"max_series": max_series, "max_points": max_points}
238	            self._save_quotas()
239	            return self.get_quota(tenant)
240	
241	    def get_quota(self, tenant):
242	        """Return limits and current usage for ``tenant`` in one snapshot."""
243	        tenant = self._clean_tenant(tenant)
244	        with self._lock:
245	            limits = self._quotas.get(tenant, {"max_series": None, "max_points": None})
246	            series = points = 0
247	            for sid, row in self._series.items():
248	                if row["tenant"] == tenant:
249	                    series += 1
250	                    points += len(self._samples[sid])
251	            return {"tenant": tenant, "max_series": limits["max_series"],
252	                    "max_points": limits["max_points"], "series": series, "points": points}
253	
254	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------- write
255	    def write(self, tenant, metric, labels, samples, now=None, overwrite=False):
256	        """Store ``samples`` = ``[(timestamp_ms, value), ...]``.
257	
258	        Idempotent: an identical ``(series, timestamp)`` value is a duplicate
259	        and changes nothing. A differing value for a stored timestamp raises
260	        ``ObsError`` unless ``overwrite=True``.
261	
262	        The whole batch is checked against the tenant's configured quotas
263	        *after* input validation and conflict rules, using the net new series
264	        and distinct new timestamps the batch would add (same-value replays,
265	        overwrites and timestamps repeated inside the batch add nothing). A
266	        batch that would exceed either limit is rejected wholesale with
267	        ``ObsError``: no series, points or write counter change is kept.
268	        """
269	        if not isinstance(samples, (list, tuple)):
270	            raise ObsError("samples must be a list of [timestamp_ms, value] pairs")
271	        clean = []
272	        for entry in samples:
273	            if not isinstance(entry, (list, tuple)) or len(entry) != 2:
274	                raise ObsError("each sample must be a [timestamp_ms, value] pair")
275	            stamp, value = entry
276	            if not _num(stamp) or not _num(value):
277	                raise ObsError("sample timestamp and value must be numbers")
278	            if now is not None and int(stamp) > int(now):
279	                raise ObsError("sample timestamp %d is in the future (now=%d)"
280	                               % (int(stamp), int(now)))
281	            clean.append((int(stamp), float(value)))
282	        if not clean:
283	            raise ObsError("samples must not be empty")
284	        # Labels/tenant are validated before the lock so conflicts and quota
285	        # breaches never surface as identity errors.
286	        pairs = _labels_list(labels)
287	        identity = canonical_identity(tenant, metric, pairs)
288	        sid = hashlib.sha256(identity.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
289	        with self._lock:
290	            existed = sid in self._series
291	            current = dict(self._samples.get(sid, ()))
292	            merged = dict(current)
293	            written = duplicates = 0
294	            new_stamps = set()
295	            overwritten = False
296	            for stamp, value in clean:
297	                if stamp in merged:
298	                    if merged[stamp] != value:
299	                        if not overwrite:
300	                            raise ObsError(
301	                                "conflict for %s at timestamp %d: stored=%r incoming=%r"
302	                                % (sid, stamp, merged[stamp], value))
303	                        if stamp in current:
304	                            overwritten = True
305	                    else:
306	                        duplicates += 1
307	                        continue
308	                else:
309	                    new_stamps.add(stamp)
310	                merged[stamp] = value
311	                written += 1
312	
313	            quota = self._quotas.get(tenant)
314	            if quota is not None:
315	                used_series = used_points = 0
316	                for sid_, row in self._series.items():
317	                    if row["tenant"] == tenant:
318	                        used_series += 1
319	                        used_points += len(self._samples[sid_])
320	                new_series = 0 if existed else 1
321	                new_points = len(new_stamps)
322	                limit_series = quota["max_series"]
323	                limit_points = quota["max_points"]
324	                if new_series and limit_series is not None \
325	                        and used_series + new_series > limit_series:
326	                    raise ObsError(
327	                        "quota exceeded for tenant %r: series %d+%d > max_series %s"
328	                        % (tenant, used_series, new_series, limit_series))
329	                if new_points and limit_points is not None \
330	                        and used_points + new_points > limit_points:
331	                    raise ObsError(
332	                        "quota exceeded for tenant %r: points %d+%d > max_points %s"
333	                        % (tenant, used_points, new_points, limit_points))
334	
335	            if not existed:
336	                self._series[sid] = {"series_id": sid, "tenant": tenant, "metric": metric,
337	                                     "labels": pairs, "identity": identity}
338	                self._samples[sid] = []
339	            if written:
340	                self._samples[sid] = sorted(merged.items())
341	                if overwritten:
342	                    # An overwrite replaced a stored value: rewrite the file so a
343	                    # timestamp never occupies more than one physical line.
344	                    self._rewrite_points(sid)
345	                else:
346	                    fresh = sorted((stamp, merged[stamp]) for stamp in new_stamps)
347	                    with open(self._points_path(sid), "a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
348	                        handle.write("".join(_line(ts, value) for ts, value in fresh))
349	                        handle.flush()
350	                        os.fsync(handle.fileno())
351	                self._writes += 1
352	                self._save_registry()
353	        return {"series_id": sid, "written": written, "duplicates": duplicates}
354	
355	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------- query
356	    def _samples_for(self, tenant, metric, labels):
357	        with self._lock:
358	            ids = sorted(sid for sid, row in self._series.items()
359	                         if row["tenant"] == tenant and row["metric"] == metric
360	                         and matches_labels(dict(row["labels"]), labels))
361	            return [(sid, list(self._samples[sid])) for sid in ids]
362	
363	    def _scan(self, tenant, metric, labels, start_ms, end_ms):
364	        """Raw samples of matching series inside ``[start, end]`` (internal).
365	
366	        Used where exact event counts matter (SLO numerator/denominator) and by
367	        rule evaluation to find candidate series.
368	        """
369	        lo = None if start_ms is None else int(start_ms)
370	        hi = None if end_ms is None else int(end_ms)
371	        out = []
372	        for sid, samples in self._samples_for(tenant, metric, labels):
373	            rows = [item for item in samples
374	                    if (lo is None or item[0] >= lo) and (hi is None or item[0] <= hi)]
375	            if rows:
376	                out.append((sid, rows))
377	        return out
378	
379	    def query(self, tenant, metric, labels=None, start_ms=None, end_ms=None,
380	              step_ms=None, agg=None, group_by=None):
381	        """Raw or bucketed points per matching series.
382	
383	        ``step_ms`` buckets are left-closed/right-open on epoch multiples and
384	        empty buckets are emitted as ``None``. A series with no sample in range
385	        is still listed, with an empty ``points`` list, unless ``agg`` is used
386	        without ``step_ms`` (then it yields nothing and is omitted).
387	
388	        ``group_by=None`` keeps this per-series behaviour. Otherwise it must
389	        be a list of distinct non-empty label keys (``[]`` merges every match
390	        into one group) and ``agg`` is required: the raw in-range samples of
391	        all series in a group are aggregated together and each result row
392	        carries only ``labels`` (the group keys present on those series) and
393	        ``points``.
394	        """
395	        if agg is not None and agg not in AGGREGATES:
396	            raise ObsError("unknown aggregation: %r" % (agg,))
397	        if step_ms is not None and (not _num(step_ms) or int(step_ms) <= 0):
398	            raise ObsError("step_ms must be a positive number")
399	        lo = None if start_ms is None else int(start_ms)
400	        hi = None if end_ms is None else int(end_ms)
401	        if lo is not None and hi is not None and hi < lo:
402	            raise ObsError("end_ms must be >= start_ms")
403	        if group_by is not None:
404	            return self._query_grouped(tenant, metric, labels, lo, hi,
405	                                       step_ms, agg, group_by)
406	        out = []
407	        for sid, samples in self._samples_for(tenant, metric, labels):
408	            rows = [item for item in samples
409	                    if (lo is None or item[0] >= lo) and (hi is None or item[0] <= hi)]
410	            points = self._bucket(rows, step_ms, agg, lo, hi)
411	            if points is None or (not points and agg is not None and step_ms is None):
412	                continue
413	            out.append({"series_id": sid, "labels": dict(self._series[sid]["labels"]),
414	                        "points": points})
415	        return out
416	
417	    def _bucket(self, rows, step_ms, agg, lo, hi):
418	        """``None`` = nothing to report, ``[]`` = known empty, else the points."""
419	        if step_ms is None:
420	            if agg is None:
421	                return [[stamp, value] for stamp, value in rows]
422	            return None if not rows else [[rows[0][0], _aggregate([v for _, v in rows], agg)]]
423	        step = int(step_ms)
424	        groups = {}
425	        for stamp, value in rows:
426	            groups.setdefault(stamp - (stamp % step), []).append(value)
427	        if not groups:
428	            return None
429	        keys = sorted(groups)
430	        start = max(keys[0], lo - (lo % step)) if lo is not None else keys[0]
431	        end = min(keys[-1], hi - (hi % step)) if hi is not None else keys[-1]
432	        return [[key, _aggregate(groups[key], agg) if key in groups else None]
433	                for key in range(start, end + 1, step)]
434	
435	    def _query_grouped(self, tenant, metric, labels, lo, hi, step_ms, agg, group_by):
436	        """Cross-series aggregation: one row per distinct ``group_by`` tuple.
437	
438	        The raw in-range samples of every series in a group are pooled before
439	        aggregating (no per-series pre-averaging), so samples from different
440	        series at the same timestamp each count. A group key absent from a
441	        series simply does not appear in that group's labels; a missing key
442	        and an empty-string value therefore land in different groups.
443	        """
444	        if not isinstance(group_by, (list, tuple)):
445	            raise ObsError("group_by must be a list of label keys")
446	        keys = list(group_by)
447	        for key in keys:
448	            if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
449	                raise ObsError("group_by entries must be non-empty strings")
450	        if len(set(keys)) != len(keys):
451	            raise ObsError("group_by entries must not contain duplicates")
452	        if agg is None:
453	            raise ObsError("group_by requires agg")
454	        groups = {}
455	        for sid, samples in self._samples_for(tenant, metric, labels):
456	            series_labels = dict(self._series[sid]["labels"])
457	            group_labels = {key: series_labels[key] for key in keys
458	                            if key in series_labels}
459	            token = tuple(sorted(group_labels.items()))
460	            entry = groups.setdefault(token, {"labels": group_labels, "rows": []})
461	            entry["rows"].extend(item for item in samples
462	                                 if (lo is None or item[0] >= lo)
463	                                 and (hi is None or item[0] <= hi))
464	        out = []
465	        for token in sorted(groups):
466	            entry = groups[token]
467	            rows = sorted(entry["rows"])
468	            if step_ms is None:
469	                points = [] if not rows else \
470	                    [[rows[0][0], _aggregate([value for _, value in rows], agg)]]
471	            else:
472	                points = self._bucket(rows, step_ms, agg, lo, hi) or []
473	            out.append({"labels": entry["labels"], "points": points})
474	        return out

476	    def rollup(self, tenant, metric, labels, window_ms, agg):
477	        """Downsampled series over the whole stored range, ordered by series_id."""
478	        if agg not in AGGREGATES:
479	            raise ObsError("unknown aggregation: %r" % (agg,))
480	        if not _num(window_ms) or int(window_ms) <= 0:
481	            raise ObsError("window_ms must be a positive number")
482	        return [{"series_id": item["series_id"], "labels": item["labels"],
483	                 "points": [point for point in item["points"] if point[1] is not None]}
484	                for item in self.query(tenant, metric, labels=labels,
485	                                       step_ms=int(window_ms), agg=agg)]
486	
487	    # --------------------------------------------------------------- retention
488	    def enforce_retention(self, tenant, cutoff_ms):
489	        """Drop every sample with ``timestamp_ms < cutoff_ms`` for ``tenant``."""
490	        cutoff = int(cutoff_ms)
491	        dropped = affected = 0
492	        with self._lock:
493	            for sid in sorted(self._series):
494	                if self._series[sid]["tenant"] != tenant:
495	                    continue
496	                keep = [item for item in self._samples[sid] if item[0] >= cutoff]
497	                removed = len(self._samples[sid]) - len(keep)
498	                if removed:
499	                    self._samples[sid] = keep
500	                    self._rewrite_points(sid)
501	                    dropped += removed
502	                    affected += 1
503	        return {"dropped": dropped, "series": affected, "cutoff_ms": cutoff}
504	
505	    def stats(self):
506	        with self._lock:
507	            per_tenant = {}
508	            points = 0
509	            for sid, row in self._series.items():
510	                count = len(self._samples[sid])
511	                points += count
512	                entry = per_tenant.setdefault(row["tenant"], {"series": 0, "points": 0})
513	                entry["series"] += 1
514	                entry["points"] += count
515	        return {"series": len(self._series), "points": points, "writes": self._writes,
516	                "tenants": per_tenant}

        if "=" not in pair:
            raise ObsError("label %r must look like key=value" % pair)
        key, value = pair.split("=", 1)
        out[key] = value
    return out
def _samples(entries):
    out = []
    for entry in entries or []:
        stamp, _, value = entry.partition(":")
        try:
            out.append([int(stamp), float(value)])
        except ValueError:
            raise ObsError("sample %r must look like timestamp_ms:value" % entry)
    if not out:
        raise ObsError("at least one --sample timestamp_ms:value is required")
    return out
def _common(parser, label_help="label matcher key=value"):
    parser.add_argument("--tenant", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--metric", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--label", action="append", default=[], help=label_help)
    return parser
def _build_parser():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="obsd",
                                     description="metrics ingestion, alerting and SLO backend")
    parser.add_argument("--data-dir", default=DEFAULT_DATA_DIR,
                        help="state directory (default ./obsd_data)")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    serve = sub.add_parser("serve", help="run the HTTP API")
    serve.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
    serve.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8080)

    quota_set = sub.add_parser("quota-set", help="set per-tenant write limits")
    quota_set.add_argument("--tenant", required=True)
    quota_set.add_argument("--max-series", type=int, default=None,
                           help="max registered series (omit for unlimited)")
    quota_set.add_argument("--max-points", type=int, default=None,
                           help="max distinct points across the tenant (omit for unlimited)")

    quota_get = sub.add_parser("quota-get", help="show a tenant's limits and usage")
    quota_get.add_argument("--tenant", required=True)

    write = _common(sub.add_parser("write", help="write samples into a series"))
    write.add_argument("--sample", action="append", default=[], metavar="TS:VALUE")
    write.add_argument("--now-ms", type=int, default=None)
    write.add_argument("--overwrite", action="store_true")

    query = _common(sub.add_parser("query", help="range query with optional bucketing"))
    query.add_argument("--start", type=int, default=None)
    query.add_argument("--end", type=int, default=None)
    query.add_argument("--step", type=int, default=None)
    query.add_argument("--agg", choices=AGGS, default=None)
    query.add_argument("--group-by", default=None, metavar="JSON_ARRAY",
                       help="JSON array of label keys for cross-series grouping "
                            "(requires --agg; [] merges all matching series)")

    rule = _common(sub.add_parser("rule-add", help="add an alert rule"))
    rule.add_argument("--id", default=None)
    rule.add_argument("--comparator", required=True, choices=COMPS)
    rule.add_argument("--threshold", type=float, required=True)
    rule.add_argument("--for-ms", type=int, default=0)
    rule.add_argument("--window-ms", type=int, required=True)
    rule.add_argument("--agg", required=True, choices=AGGS)
    rule.add_argument("--severity", required=True, choices=SEVERITIES)
    rule.add_argument("--annotation", action="append", default=[])

    evaluate = sub.add_parser("eval", help="evaluate all rules at a timestamp")
    evaluate.add_argument("--now-ms", type=int, required=True)

    alerts = sub.add_parser("alerts", help="list alerts")
    alerts.add_argument("--tenant", default=None)
    alerts.add_argument("--state", default=None)

    silence = sub.add_parser("silence-add", help="add a silence window")
    silence.add_argument("--tenant", required=True)
    silence.add_argument("--label", action="append", default=[])
    silence.add_argument("--starts-ms", type=int, required=True)
    silence.add_argument("--ends-ms", type=int, required=True)
    silence.add_argument("--reason", default="")

    slo = sub.add_parser("slo", help="SLO management")
    slo_sub = slo.add_subparsers(dest="slo_command", required=True)
    slo_set = _common(slo_sub.add_parser("set"))
    slo_set.add_argument("--name", required=True)
    slo_set.add_argument("--good-comparator", required=True, choices=COMPS)
    slo_set.add_argument("--threshold", type=float, required=True)
    slo_set.add_argument("--target-ratio", type=float, required=True)
    slo_set.add_argument("--window-ms", type=int, required=True)
    slo_status = slo_sub.add_parser("status")
    slo_status.add_argument("--name", required=True)
    slo_status.add_argument("--tenant", default=None)
    slo_status.add_argument("--now-ms", type=int, required=True)
    return parser
def _run(args, store, engine):
    if args.command == "serve":
        return run_server(store, engine, args.host, args.port)
    if args.command == "quota-set":
        _emit(store.set_quota(args.tenant, args.max_series, args.max_points))
    elif args.command == "quota-get":
        _emit(store.get_quota(args.tenant))
    elif args.command == "write":
        _emit(store.write(args.tenant, args.metric, _labels(args.label),
                          _samples(args.sample), now=args.now_ms, overwrite=args.overwrite))
    elif args.command == "query":
        group_by = None
        if args.group_by is not None:
            try:
                group_by = json.loads(args.group_by)
            except ValueError:
                raise ObsError("--group-by must be a JSON array of label keys")
        rows = store.query(args.tenant, args.metric, labels=_labels(args.label),
                           start_ms=args.start, end_ms=args.end, step_ms=args.step,
                           agg=args.agg, group_by=group_by)
        _emit({"series": [{"labels": row["labels"], "points": row["points"]} for row in rows]})
    elif args.command == "rule-add":
        _emit(engine.add_rule({
            "id": args.id, "tenant": args.tenant, "metric": args.metric,
            "labels": _labels(args.label), "comparator": args.comparator,
            "threshold": args.threshold, "for_ms": args.for_ms, "window_ms": args.window_ms,
            "agg": args.agg, "severity": args.severity,
            "annotations": _labels(args.annotation)}))
    elif args.command == "eval":
        _emit(engine.evaluate(args.now_ms))
    elif args.command == "alerts":
        _emit({"alerts": engine.list_alerts(args.tenant, args.state)})
    elif args.command == "silence-add":
        _emit(engine.add_silence(args.tenant, _labels(args.label), args.starts_ms,
                                 args.ends_ms, args.reason))
    elif args.command == "slo" and args.slo_command == "set":
        _emit(engine.set_slo(args.tenant, args.name, args.metric, _labels(args.label),
                             args.good_comparator, args.threshold, args.target_ratio,
                             args.window_ms))
    elif args.command == "slo":
        _emit(engine.slo_status(args.name, args.now_ms, tenant=args.tenant))
    else:
        return _fail("unknown command: %s" % args.command)
    return 0
def main(argv=None):
    """Dispatch one CLI invocation; 0 on success, non-zero + JSON error otherwise."""
    parser = _build_parser()
    try:
        args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    except SystemExit as exc:
        return _fail("invalid arguments (exit %s)" % exc.code)
    try:
        data_dir = os.path.abspath(args.data_dir)
        store = SeriesStore(data_dir)
        return _run(args, store, AlertEngine(store, data_dir))
    except ObsError as exc:
        return _fail(exc)
    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
        return _fail("%s: %s" % (type(exc).__name__, exc))
if __name__ == "__main__":  # pragma: no cover
    sys.exit(main())

1	# obsd
2	
3	Minimal, dependency-free backend skeleton for **metrics ingestion, alerting and
4	SLO tracking**. Python 3.10+, standard library only, offline, deterministic
5	(every time-dependent entry point takes an injected `now_ms`).
6	
7	The lane goal is a metrics collection, alerting and SLO backend that grows
8	towards time-series writes and downsampling, label indexing and a query subset,
9	aggregation and sliding windows, alert rules with silencing and inhibition,
10	notification routing and dedup, SLO and error-budget math, retention and
11	compaction, multi-tenant quota, access control and audit, and consistent reads
12	under high availability. This seed implements the first, smallest *real* slice of
13	each of those areas.
14	
15	## Run
16	
17	```bash
18	# HTTP API (data dir flag is global and comes BEFORE the subcommand)
19	python3 -m obsd --data-dir ./obsd_data serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080
20	
21	# test suite
22	python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
23	```
24	
25	Both commands are run offline with the system interpreter; no third-party
26	package is imported anywhere.
27	
28	## CLI
29	
30	`python3 -m obsd [--data-dir ./obsd_data] <command> ...` prints exactly one line
31	of JSON on stdout. On error it prints one line of JSON (`{"error":"..."}`) on
32	stderr and exits non-zero.
33	
34	| Command | Example |
35	| --- | --- |
36	| `serve` | `python3 -m obsd --data-dir ./obsd_data serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080` |
37	| `quota-set` | `python3 -m obsd quota-set --tenant acme --max-series 1000 --max-points 1000000` |
38	| `quota-get` | `python3 -m obsd quota-get --tenant acme` |
39	| `write` | `python3 -m obsd write --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --label host=a --sample 1000:12.5 --now-ms 2000` |
40	| `query` | `python3 -m obsd query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --start 0 --end 5000 --step 1000 --agg avg` |
41	| `query` (grouped) | `python3 -m obsd query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --agg avg --group-by '["host"]'` |
42	| `rule-add` | `python3 -m obsd rule-add --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --comparator "<" --threshold 10 --window-ms 60000 --for-ms 30000 --agg avg --severity warning` |
43	| `eval` | `python3 -m obsd eval --now-ms 68000` |
44	| `alerts` | `python3 -m obsd alerts --tenant acme --state firing` |
45	| `silence-add` | `python3 -m obsd silence-add --tenant acme --starts-ms 0 --ends-ms 90000 --reason maintenance` |
46	| `slo set` | `python3 -m obsd slo set --tenant acme --name availability --metric latency_ms --good-comparator ">=" --threshold 1 --target-ratio 0.9 --window-ms 60000` |
47	| `slo status` | `python3 -m obsd slo status --name availability --now-ms 60000` |
48	
49	## HTTP API
50	
51	Errors are always JSON: `{"error":"..."}` with status 400 (bad request),
52	404 (unknown resource) or 409 (write conflict or quota exceeded).
53	
54	| Method | Path | Request | Response |
55	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
56	| GET | `/healthz` | – | `200 {"ok":true}` |
57	| POST | `/v1/series` | `{"tenant","metric","labels","samples":[[ts,value],...]}` | `202 {"written":n,"duplicates":m,"series_id":"..."}`, `409` on conflicting timestamp or quota exceeded |
58	| GET | `/v1/query` | `?tenant=&metric=&label.k=v&start=&end=&step=&agg=&group_by=` (group_by is a JSON array of label keys) | `200 {"series":[{"labels":{...},"points":[[ts,value\|null],...]}]}` |
59	| POST | `/v1/quotas` | `{"tenant","max_series":n\|null,"max_points":n\|null}` | `200 {"tenant","max_series","max_points","series","points"}`; invalid tenant/limits give `400` and leave config untouched |
60	| GET | `/v1/quotas` | `?tenant=` | `200 {"tenant","max_series","max_points","series","points"}` (unconfigured tenant reports `null` limits and real usage) |
61	| POST | `/v1/rules` | rule object | `201` stored rule |
62	| GET | `/v1/rules` | `?tenant=` | `200 {"rules":[...]}` |
63	| POST | `/v1/evaluate` | `{"now_ms":n}` | `200 {"firing":[...],"silenced":[...],"inhibited":[...],"resolved":[...]}` |
64	| GET | `/v1/alerts` | `?tenant=&state=` | `200 {"alerts":[...]}` |
65	| POST | `/v1/silences` | `{"tenant","labels","starts_ms","ends_ms","reason"}` | `201` stored silence |
66	| POST | `/v1/inhibitions` | `{"source_severity","target_severity","same_labels"}` | `201` stored inhibition |
67	| POST | `/v1/slos` | `{"tenant","name","metric","labels","good_comparator","threshold","target_ratio","window_ms"}` | `201` stored SLO |
68	| GET | `/v1/slos/status` | `?tenant=&name=&now_ms=` | `200` SLO status object |
69	| GET | `/v1/stats` | – | `200 {"store":{...},"alerts":n}` |
70	
71	## Data model
72	
73	A series identity is `(tenant, metric, sorted(label pairs))`. The canonical
74	identity string joins the tenant, the metric and every `key=value` label pair
75	(sorted by key) with `\n`:
76	
77	```
78	acme\nlatency_ms\nhost=a\nregion=eu
79	```
80	
81	`series_id = sha256(canonical_identity).hexdigest()`, so the same logical series
82	always maps to the same 64-character id, independent of label insertion order.
83	
84	Storage layout (all writes atomic via temp file + `os.replace`):
85	
86	```
87	<data-dir>/series.json              registry: series_id -> tenant/metric/labels
88	<data-dir>/points/<series_id>.jsonl one {"t":ts,"v":value} object per line
89	<data-dir>/quotas.json              tenant -> {"max_series","max_points"} limits
90	<data-dir>/rules.json               <data-dir>/alerts.json
91	<data-dir>/slos.json                <data-dir>/silences.json
92	<data-dir>/inhibitions.json         <data-dir>/counters.json
93	```
94	
95	A directory written before quotas existed simply has no `quotas.json`, which
96	means every tenant is unlimited; limits and usage are reloaded together on
97	construction so a reopen always reports a consistent snapshot.
98	
99	`SeriesStore` and `AlertEngine` each guard their state with a
100	`threading.RLock`, so the threaded HTTP server can serve concurrent requests; all
101	state is reloaded from disk on construction, so a restart preserves series,
102	points, rules, alerts, silences, inhibitions and SLOs.
103	
104	## Semantics and formulas
105	
106	**Idempotent write.** `write(tenant, metric, labels, samples, now=None,
107	overwrite=False)` stores `(timestamp_ms, value)` pairs. Writing an existing
108	`(series, timestamp)` with the *same* value is a duplicate: it changes nothing
109	and is counted in `duplicates`. A *different* value for a stored timestamp is a
110	conflict: it raises `ObsError` (`409` over HTTP) unless `overwrite=True`, in
111	which case the stored value is replaced and counted in `written`. A timestamp
112	greater than the injected `now` (when `now` is given) is rejected.
113	
114	**Bucketing.** `query(..., step_ms=step, agg=agg)` assigns a sample with
115	timestamp `t` to bucket `b = t - (t % step)`, i.e. buckets are
116	left-closed/right-open (`[b, b+step)`) on epoch multiples. Every bucket from the
117	first non-empty bucket to the last non-empty bucket that also lies inside
118	`[start_ms, end_ms]` is emitted, and buckets with no sample are emitted as
119	`[b, null]`. Bucket value = `agg` over the samples in the bucket, where `agg` is
120	one of `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `count`. A series whose range contains no
121	sample is still listed with an empty `points` list. With `agg` and *no*
122	`step_ms` the whole `[start_ms, end_ms]` range is a single bucket. With neither,
123	raw samples are returned in `[timestamp, value]` order. `rollup(tenant, metric,
124	labels, window_ms, agg)` is `query` with `step_ms = window_ms` over the whole
125	stored range, with empty buckets dropped; output is ordered by `series_id`, so
126	it is deterministic.
127	
128	**Grouped query.** `query(..., agg=agg, group_by=[keys...])` aggregates *across*
129	series: matching series (same tenant/metric/label filters and `[start_ms,
130	end_ms]` range as above) are bucketed into groups by the values of the given
131	label keys, and the raw in-range samples of all series in a group are pooled
132	before `agg` is applied — samples from different series at the same timestamp
133	count individually. `group_by=[]` merges every matching series into one group.
134	Each result row carries only `labels` (the group keys actually present on the
135	group's series — a missing key and an empty-string value form different
136	groups) and `points`; rows are ordered lexicographically by their sorted label
137	pairs. Bucketing follows the same rules as the per-series query (epoch-aligned
138	left-closed buckets with `null` gaps, or a single point at the group's
139	earliest sample without `step_ms`). A group whose series have no sample in
140	range is still listed with empty `points`; no matching series at all yields an
141	empty `series` array. `group_by` must be a list of distinct non-empty strings
142	and requires `agg`; violations raise `ObsError` (`400` over HTTP, one JSON
143	error line on stderr for the CLI).
144	
145	**Retention.** `enforce_retention(tenant, cutoff_ms)` removes every sample of
146	that tenant with `timestamp_millis < cutoff_ms` and rewrites the affected point
147	files. `stats()` returns `{"series","points","writes","tenants"}`.
148	
149	**Per-tenant quotas.** `set_quota(tenant, max_series, max_points)` sets the
150	tenant-wide limits; each limit is a non-negative integer or `null` (omitted
151	fields over HTTP also mean `null`, i.e. unlimited), and `0` forbids adding any.
152	`get_quota(tenant)` returns
153	`{"tenant","max_series","max_points","series","points"}` — the configured
154	limits and the current usage in one snapshot. Configuring a quota never creates
155	a series, and an unconfigured tenant is unlimited. Limits apply to all of a
156	tenant's metrics together: `series` is the number of registered series and
157	`points` the total number of *distinct timestamps* across those series, not
158	physical point-file lines. Label order, same-value replays, overwritten points
159	and a timestamp repeated inside one batch add no occupancy.
160	
161	Every write path (`SeriesStore.write`, `POST /v1/series`, the CLI `write`) is
162	checked after the existing input validation and conflict rules, using the
163	batch's net increase: a batch is rejected (ObsError / HTTP `409` / CLI JSON
164	error with non-zero exit) when *either* dimension it increases would exceed its
165	limit, and the rejection leaves no new series, samples or write-count change.
166	Limits may be lowered below current usage; afterwards only the dimensions a
167	write actually increases are checked — an already-over-limit dimension blocks
168	nothing by itself, so pure duplicates and overwrites keep succeeding. Retention
169	frees the occupancy of deleted points, while empty series stay registered.
170	Overwrites rewrite the point file so one timestamp never occupies two lines; on
171	reopen, any duplicate timestamp lines (including those left by older builds)
172	collapse to the last value, so historical re-overwrites never double-count.
173	
174	**Rule shape.** `{"id","tenant","metric","labels","comparator" ∈ {">",">=","<",
175	"<=","==","!="},"threshold","for_ms","window_ms","agg","severity" ∈ {"info",
176	"warning","critical"},"annotations"}`. `add_rule` validates every field and
177	raises `ObsError` for anything malformed (`id` is generated when omitted).
178	
179	**Evaluation window.** Let `step = window_ms`, `t = now_ms` and
180	`bucket_start(t) = t - (t % step)`. The window is
181	`[bucket_start(t) - step, t]`, i.e. the current bucket plus the whole previous
182	bucket. The rule condition holds for a series when *every* non-empty bucket in
183	that window satisfies `comparator(value, threshold)` — one violating bucket
184	anywhere in the window stops the condition, and it keeps stopping it until that
185	bucket has left the window.
186	
187	**`for_ms`.** Let `run_start` be the timestamp of the first bucket of the
188	current unbroken run of satisfying buckets (a violating bucket resets the run).
189	The rule fires only when the condition holds *and*
190	`bucket_start(now_ms) - run_start >= for_ms`. With `for_ms = 0`, one satisfied
191	bucket is enough; with `for_ms = window_ms`, the current and the previous bucket
192	must both be satisfied. Before the hold time is reached the alert is recorded
193	with `firing = false` and appears in none of the four output lists.
194	
195	**Alert identity and dedup.** Alert identity is `(rule_id, series_id)`, distinct
196	from the alert id. The first time a condition holds an alert id
197	`alert-NNNNN` is minted for that identity and reused forever: re-evaluating an
198	unchanged condition returns the *same* `id` and increments `occurrences` (the
199	number of evaluations in which the condition held). `since_ms` is `run_start`,
200	not the evaluation time, so dedup does not depend on the wall clock.
201	
202	**Resolution.** When the condition stops holding, the alert's state becomes
203	`resolved`, `firing` becomes `false`, `resolved_ms` is set once, and the alert is
204	reported in the `resolved` list of that evaluation. If the same condition holds
205	again later, the *same alert id* is reused and `occurrences` keeps counting.
206	Because the condition covers the whole window, a series that produced one bad
207	bucket stays unresolved until that bucket has left the window.
208	
209	**Silence vs inhibition precedence.** A condition that holds and whose `for_ms`
210	is satisfied is first checked against active silences: a silence is active when
211	`starts_ms <= now_ms <= ends_ms`, the tenant matches and every silence label
212	matcher is present in the series labels. Inside an active silence the alert state
213	is `silenced` (it is *not* firing) and the silence id and reason are recorded.
214	Only if no silence matches is inhibition checked: an inhibition
215	`(source_severity, target_severity, same_labels)` marks a `target_severity` alert
216	as `inhibited` while an alert of at least `source_severity` is currently
217	`firing` in the same tenant with *exactly the same label set*. Silence therefore
218	wins over inhibition. A silenced or inhibited alert still counts its
219	`occurrences` and returns to `firing` as soon as the silence/inhibition no longer
220	applies. `list_alerts(state=None)` filters by `firing`, `silenced`, `inhibited`
221	or `resolved`.
222	
223	**SLO and error budget.** `set_slo(tenant, name, metric, labels,
224	good_comparator, threshold, target_ratio, window_ms)` defines a good-events
225	ratio SLO. `slo_status(name, now_ms, tenant=None)` counts every stored sample of
226	the matching series inside `[now_ms - window_ms, now_ms]`:
227	
228	```
229	total          = number of samples in the window (nulls excluded)
230	good           = samples where compare(value, good_comparator, threshold)
231	bad            = total - good
232	ratio          = good / total                             (0.0 when total == 0)
233	error_budget   = max(0.0, 1 - (1 - ratio) / (1 - target_ratio))   (target_ratio < 1)
234	               = 1.0 if ratio >= 1.0 else 0.0              (target_ratio == 1)
235	burn_rate      = (bad / total) / (1 - target_ratio)        (0.0 when target_ratio >= 1 or total == 0)
236	met            = ratio >= target_ratio
237	```
238	
239	`ratio` is the observed good ratio, `target_ratio ∈ (0,1]` the objective,
240	`burn_rate` how fast the budget is being spent relative to the allowed bad rate
241	(`1.0` means exactly on budget, `> 1.0` means burning too fast) and
242	`error_budget` the *fraction of the allowed error budget still unspent*:
243	`1.0` means untouched, `0.0` means exhausted or exceeded. For any `ratio` that
244	meets the target the two written forms of `error_budget` are identical, since
245	`1 - (1-ratio)/(1-target) = (ratio - target)/(1 - target)` and
246	`1 - ratio/target = (target - ratio)/target` are both non-negative only inside
247	their own regime; the first form is the one used, because it degrades sensibly
248	when the ratio beats the target (more budget left) instead of pinning to `0`.
249	With `total == 0` the ratio is `0.0`, so the budget counts as exhausted.
250	
251	Examples: 9 good + 1 bad with `target_ratio = 0.9` gives `ratio = 0.9`,
252	`error_budget = 0.0`, `burn_rate = 0.1/0.1 = 1.0`, `met = true` (exactly on
253	budget). 98 good + 2 bad with `target_ratio = 0.95` gives `ratio = 0.98`,
254	`burn_rate = 0.02/0.05 = 0.4` and `error_budget = 1 - 0.02/0.05 = 0.6` (60% of
255	the budget still unspent). 90 good + 10 bad with `target_ratio = 0.99` gives
256	`ratio = 0.9`, `burn_rate = 10.0`, `error_budget = 0.0`, `met = false`.
257	
258	**Determinism.** No module calls `time.time()` inside decision logic: `now_ms` is
259	passed into `evaluate`, `slo_status` and `write` (the HTTP layer uses the wall
260	clock only when a caller omits `now_ms` on `GET /v1/slos/status`, and
261	`/v1/slos/status` requires it in the CLI).
262	
263	## Layout
264	
265	```
266	obsd/__init__.py    public exports
267	obsd/tsdb.py        SeriesStore
268	obsd/alerts.py      AlertEngine
269	obsd/http_app.py    ThreadingHTTPServer + create_server
270	obsd/cli.py         command line interface
271	obsd/__main__.py    python3 -m obsd entry point
272	tests/              unittest suite (tsdb, alerts, http)
273	```

# obsd

Minimal, dependency-free backend skeleton for **metrics ingestion, alerting and
SLO tracking**. Python 3.10+, standard library only, offline, deterministic
(every time-dependent entry point takes an injected `now_ms`).

The lane goal is a metrics collection, alerting and SLO backend that grows
towards time-series writes and downsampling, label indexing and a query subset,
aggregation and sliding windows, alert rules with silencing and inhibition,
notification routing and dedup, SLO and error-budget math, retention and
compaction, multi-tenant quota, access control and audit, and consistent reads
under high availability. This seed implements the first, smallest *real* slice of
each of those areas.

## Run

```bash
# HTTP API (data dir flag is global and comes BEFORE the subcommand)
python3 -m obsd --data-dir ./obsd_data serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080

# test suite
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Both commands are run offline with the system interpreter; no third-party
package is imported anywhere.

## CLI

`python3 -m obsd [--data-dir ./obsd_data] <command> ...` prints exactly one line
of JSON on stdout. On error it prints one line of JSON (`{"error":"..."}`) on
stderr and exits non-zero.

| Command | Example |
| --- | --- |
| `serve` | `python3 -m obsd --data-dir ./obsd_data serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080` |
| `quota-set` | `python3 -m obsd quota-set --tenant acme --max-series 1000 --max-points 1000000` |
| `quota-get` | `python3 -m obsd quota-get --tenant acme` |
| `write` | `python3 -m obsd write --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --label host=a --sample 1000:12.5 --now-ms 2000` |
| `query` | `python3 -m obsd query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --start 0 --end 5000 --step 1000 --agg avg` |
| `query` (grouped) | `python3 -m obsd query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --agg avg --group-by '["host"]'` |
| `rule-add` | `python3 -m obsd rule-add --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --comparator "<" --threshold 10 --window-ms 60000 --for-ms 30000 --agg avg --severity warning` |
| `eval` | `python3 -m obsd eval --now-ms 68000` |
| `alerts` | `python3 -m obsd alerts --tenant acme --state firing` |
| `silence-add` | `python3 -m obsd silence-add --tenant acme --starts-ms 0 --ends-ms 90000 --reason maintenance` |
| `slo set` | `python3 -m obsd slo set --tenant acme --name availability --metric latency_ms --good-comparator ">=" --threshold 1 --target-ratio 0.9 --window-ms 60000` |
| `slo status` | `python3 -m obsd slo status --name availability --now-ms 60000` |

## HTTP API

Errors are always JSON: `{"error":"..."}` with status 400 (bad request),
404 (unknown resource) or 409 (write conflict or quota exceeded).

| Method | Path | Request | Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/healthz` | – | `200 {"ok":true}` |
| POST | `/v1/series` | `{"tenant","metric","labels","samples":[[ts,value],...]}` | `202 {"written":n,"duplicates":m,"series_id":"..."}`, `409` on conflicting timestamp or quota exceeded |
| GET | `/v1/query` | `?tenant=&metric=&label.k=v&start=&end=&step=&agg=&group_by=` (group_by is a JSON array of label keys) | `200 {"series":[{"labels":{...},"points":[[ts,value\|null],...]}]}` |
| POST | `/v1/quotas` | `{"tenant","max_series":n\|null,"max_points":n\|null}` | `200 {"tenant","max_series","max_points","series","points"}`; invalid tenant/limits give `400` and leave config untouched |
| GET | `/v1/quotas` | `?tenant=` | `200 {"tenant","max_series","max_points","series","points"}` (unconfigured tenant reports `null` limits and real usage) |
| POST | `/v1/rules` | rule object | `201` stored rule |
| GET | `/v1/rules` | `?tenant=` | `200 {"rules":[...]}` |
| POST | `/v1/evaluate` | `{"now_ms":n}` | `200 {"firing":[...],"silenced":[...],"inhibited":[...],"resolved":[...]}` |
| GET | `/v1/alerts` | `?tenant=&state=` | `200 {"alerts":[...]}` |
| POST | `/v1/silences` | `{"tenant","labels","starts_ms","ends_ms","reason"}` | `201` stored silence |
| POST | `/v1/inhibitions` | `{"source_severity","target_severity","same_labels"}` | `201` stored inhibition |
| POST | `/v1/slos` | `{"tenant","name","metric","labels","good_comparator","threshold","target_ratio","window_ms"}` | `201` stored SLO |
| GET | `/v1/slos/status` | `?tenant=&name=&now_ms=` | `200` SLO status object |
| GET | `/v1/stats` | – | `200 {"store":{...},"alerts":n}` |

## Data model

A series identity is `(tenant, metric, sorted(label pairs))`. The canonical
identity string joins the tenant, the metric and every `key=value` label pair
(sorted by key) with `\n`:

```
acme\nlatency_ms\nhost=a\nregion=eu
```

`series_id = sha256(canonical_identity).hexdigest()`, so the same logical series
always maps to the same 64-character id, independent of label insertion order.

Storage layout (all writes atomic via temp file + `os.replace`):

```
<data-dir>/series.json              registry: series_id -> tenant/metric/labels
<data-dir>/points/<series_id>.jsonl one {"t":ts,"v":value} object per line
<data-dir>/quotas.json              tenant -> {"max_series","max_points"} limits
<data-dir>/rules.json               <data-dir>/alerts.json
<data-dir>/slos.json                <data-dir>/silences.json
<data-dir>/inhibitions.json         <data-dir>/counters.json
```

A directory written before quotas existed simply has no `quotas.json`, which
means every tenant is unlimited; limits and usage are reloaded together on
construction so a reopen always reports a consistent snapshot.

`SeriesStore` and `AlertEngine` each guard their state with a
`threading.RLock`, so the threaded HTTP server can serve concurrent requests; all
state is reloaded from disk on construction, so a restart preserves series,
points, rules, alerts, silences, inhibitions and SLOs.

## Semantics and formulas

**Idempotent write.** `write(tenant, metric, labels, samples, now=None,
overwrite=False)` stores `(timestamp_ms, value)` pairs. Writing an existing
`(series, timestamp)` with the *same* value is a duplicate: it changes nothing
and is counted in `duplicates`. A *different* value for a stored timestamp is a
conflict: it raises `ObsError` (`409` over HTTP) unless `overwrite=True`, in
which case the stored value is replaced and counted in `written`. A timestamp
greater than the injected `now` (when `now` is given) is rejected.

**Bucketing.** `query(..., step_ms=step, agg=agg)` assigns a sample with
timestamp `t` to bucket `b = t - (t % step)`, i.e. buckets are
left-closed/right-open (`[b, b+step)`) on epoch multiples. Every bucket from the
first non-empty bucket to the last non-empty bucket that also lies inside
`[start_ms, end_ms]` is emitted, and buckets with no sample are emitted as
`[b, null]`. Bucket value = `agg` over the samples in the bucket, where `agg` is
one of `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `count`. A series whose range contains no
sample is still listed with an empty `points` list. With `agg` and *no*
`step_ms` the whole `[start_ms, end_ms]` range is a single bucket. With neither,
raw samples are returned in `[timestamp, value]` order. `rollup(tenant, metric,
labels, window_ms, agg)` is `query` with `step_ms = window_ms` over the whole
stored range, with empty buckets dropped; output is ordered by `series_id`, so
it is deterministic.

**Grouped query.** `query(..., agg=agg, group_by=[keys...])` aggregates *across*
series: matching series (same tenant/metric/label filters and `[start_ms,
end_ms]` range as above) are bucketed into groups by the values of the given
label keys, and the raw in-range samples of all series in a group are pooled
before `agg` is applied — samples from different series at the same timestamp
count individually. `group_by=[]` merges every matching series into one group.
Each result row carries only `labels` (the group keys actually present on the
group's series — a missing key and an empty-string value form different
groups) and `points`; rows are ordered lexicographically by their sorted label
pairs. Bucketing follows the same rules as the per-series query (epoch-aligned
left-closed buckets with `null` gaps, or a single point at the group's
earliest sample without `step_ms`). A group whose series have no sample in
range is still listed with empty `points`; no matching series at all yields an
empty `series` array. `group_by` must be a list of distinct non-empty strings
and requires `agg`; violations raise `ObsError` (`400` over HTTP, one JSON
error line on stderr for the CLI).

**Retention.** `enforce_retention(tenant, cutoff_ms)` removes every sample of
that tenant with `timestamp_millis < cutoff_ms` and rewrites the affected point
files. `stats()` returns `{"series","points","writes","tenants"}`.

**Per-tenant quotas.** `set_quota(tenant, max_series, max_points)` sets the
tenant-wide limits; each limit is a non-negative integer or `null` (omitted
fields over HTTP also mean `null`, i.e. unlimited), and `0` forbids adding any.
`get_quota(tenant)` returns
`{"tenant","max_series","max_points","series","points"}` — the configured
limits and the current usage in one snapshot. Configuring a quota never creates
a series, and an unconfigured tenant is unlimited. Limits apply to all of a
tenant's metrics together: `series` is the number of registered series and
`points` the total number of *distinct timestamps* across those series, not
physical point-file lines. Label order, same-value replays, overwritten points
and a timestamp repeated inside one batch add no occupancy.

Every write path (`SeriesStore.write`, `POST /v1/series`, the CLI `write`) is
checked after the existing input validation and conflict rules, using the
batch's net increase: a batch is rejected (ObsError / HTTP `409` / CLI JSON
error with non-zero exit) when *either* dimension it increases would exceed its
limit, and the rejection leaves no new series, samples or write-count change.
Limits may be lowered below current usage; afterwards only the dimensions a
write actually increases are checked — an already-over-limit dimension blocks
nothing by itself, so pure duplicates and overwrites keep succeeding. Retention
frees the occupancy of deleted points, while empty series stay registered.
Overwrites rewrite the point file so one timestamp never occupies two lines; on
reopen, any duplicate timestamp lines (including those left by older builds)
collapse to the last value, so historical re-overwrites never double-count.

**Rule shape.** `{"id","tenant","metric","labels","comparator" ∈ {">",">=","<",
"<=","==","!="},"threshold","for_ms","window_ms","agg","severity" ∈ {"info",
"warning","critical"},"annotations"}`. `add_rule` validates every field and
raises `ObsError` for anything malformed (`id` is generated when omitted).

**Evaluation window.** Let `step = window_ms`, `t = now_ms` and
`bucket_start(t) = t - (t % step)`. The window is
`[bucket_start(t) - step, t]`, i.e. the current bucket plus the whole previous
bucket. The rule condition holds for a series when *every* non-empty bucket in
that window satisfies `comparator(value, threshold)` — one violating bucket
anywhere in the window stops the condition, and it keeps stopping it until that
bucket has left the window.

**`for_ms`.** Let `run_start` be the timestamp of the first bucket of the
current unbroken run of satisfying buckets (a violating bucket resets the run).
The rule fires only when the condition holds *and*
`bucket_start(now_ms) - run_start >= for_ms`. With `for_ms = 0`, one satisfied
bucket is enough; with `for_ms = window_ms`, the current and the previous bucket
must both be satisfied. Before the hold time is reached the alert is recorded
with `firing = false` and appears in none of the four output lists.

**Alert identity and dedup.** Alert identity is `(rule_id, series_id)`, distinct
from the alert id. The first time a condition holds an alert id
`alert-NNNNN` is minted for that identity and reused forever: re-evaluating an
unchanged condition returns the *same* `id` and increments `occurrences` (the
number of evaluations in which the condition held). `since_ms` is `run_start`,
not the evaluation time, so dedup does not depend on the wall clock.

**Resolution.** When the condition stops holding, the alert's state becomes
`resolved`, `firing` becomes `false`, `resolved_ms` is set once, and the alert is
reported in the `resolved` list of that evaluation. If the same condition holds
again later, the *same alert id* is reused and `occurrences` keeps counting.
Because the condition covers the whole window, a series that produced one bad
bucket stays unresolved until that bucket has left the window.

**Silence vs inhibition precedence.** A condition that holds and whose `for_ms`
is satisfied is first checked against active silences: a silence is active when
`starts_ms <= now_ms <= ends_ms`, the tenant matches and every silence label
matcher is present in the series labels. Inside an active silence the alert state
is `silenced` (it is *not* firing) and the silence id and reason are recorded.
Only if no silence matches is inhibition checked: an inhibition
`(source_severity, target_severity, same_labels)` marks a `target_severity` alert
as `inhibited` while an alert of at least `source_severity` is currently
`firing` in the same tenant with *exactly the same label set*. Silence therefore
wins over inhibition. A silenced or inhibited alert still counts its
`occurrences` and returns to `firing` as soon as the silence/inhibition no longer
applies. `list_alerts(state=None)` filters by `firing`, `silenced`, `inhibited`
or `resolved`.

**SLO and error budget.** `set_slo(tenant, name, metric, labels,
good_comparator, threshold, target_ratio, window_ms)` defines a good-events
ratio SLO. `slo_status(name, now_ms, tenant=None)` counts every stored sample of
the matching series inside `[now_ms - window_ms, now_ms]`:

```
total          = number of samples in the window (nulls excluded)
good           = samples where compare(value, good_comparator, threshold)
bad            = total - good
ratio          = good / total                             (0.0 when total == 0)
error_budget   = max(0.0, 1 - (1 - ratio) / (1 - target_ratio))   (target_ratio < 1)
               = 1.0 if ratio >= 1.0 else 0.0              (target_ratio == 1)
burn_rate      = (bad / total) / (1 - target_ratio)        (0.0 when target_ratio >= 1 or total == 0)
met            = ratio >= target_ratio
```

`ratio` is the observed good ratio, `target_ratio ∈ (0,1]` the objective,
`burn_rate` how fast the budget is being spent relative to the allowed bad rate
(`1.0` means exactly on budget, `> 1.0` means burning too fast) and
`error_budget` the *fraction of the allowed error budget still unspent*:
`1.0` means untouched, `0.0` means exhausted or exceeded. For any `ratio` that
meets the target the two written forms of `error_budget` are identical, since
`1 - (1-ratio)/(1-target) = (ratio - target)/(1 - target)` and
`1 - ratio/target = (target - ratio)/target` are both non-negative only inside
their own regime; the first form is the one used, because it degrades sensibly
when the ratio beats the target (more budget left) instead of pinning to `0`.
With `total == 0` the ratio is `0.0`, so the budget counts as exhausted.

Examples: 9 good + 1 bad with `target_ratio = 0.9` gives `ratio = 0.9`,
`error_budget = 0.0`, `burn_rate = 0.1/0.1 = 1.0`, `met = true` (exactly on
budget). 98 good + 2 bad with `target_ratio = 0.95` gives `ratio = 0.98`,
`burn_rate = 0.02/0.05 = 0.4` and `error_budget = 1 - 0.02/0.05 = 0.6` (60% of
the budget still unspent). 90 good + 10 bad with `target_ratio = 0.99` gives
`ratio = 0.9`, `burn_rate = 10.0`, `error_budget = 0.0`, `met = false`.

**Determinism.** No module calls `time.time()` inside decision logic: `now_ms` is
passed into `evaluate`, `slo_status` and `write` (the HTTP layer uses the wall
clock only when a caller omits `now_ms` on `GET /v1/slos/status`, and
`/v1/slos/status` requires it in the CLI).

## Layout

```
obsd/__init__.py    public exports
obsd/tsdb.py        SeriesStore
obsd/alerts.py      AlertEngine
obsd/http_app.py    ThreadingHTTPServer + create_server
obsd/cli.py         command line interface
obsd/__main__.py    python3 -m obsd entry point
tests/              unittest suite (tsdb, alerts, http)
```

## Tests

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Covered: series identity and label-order independence, idempotent re-write,
conflicting-timestamp rejection and `overwrite`, range filtering, epoch-aligned
buckets, null buckets, all five aggregations, deterministic rollups, retention,
restart safety, rule validation, `for_ms` timing, dedup with occurrence
counting, resolution and re-firing (including the window that keeps a bad bucket
blocking), silence scoping and expiry, inhibition by severity and exact label
set, SLO/error-budget/burn-rate math (including the empty window), quota
configuration/validation, net-increase enforcement and whole-batch rejection,
zero/lowered limits with duplicates and overwrites, tenant isolation, quota
release under retention, quota/usage consistency after reopen (including
collapsed duplicate timestamp lines), concurrent writes/reconfiguration/pruning,
and the live HTTP surface over a real socket.

Everything is deterministic: the suite injects every timestamp it uses, and the
modules never read the wall clock inside decision logic.

15	class HttpCase(unittest.TestCase):
16	    def setUp(self):
17	        self.tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="obsd-http-")
18	        root = os.path.join(self.tmp, "data")
19	        self.store = SeriesStore(root)
20	        self.engine = AlertEngine(self.store, root)
21	        self.server = create_server(self.store, self.engine, "127.0.0.1", 0)
22	        self.base = "http://127.0.0.1:%d" % self.server.server_address[1]
23	        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
24	        self.thread.start()
25	    def tearDown(self):
26	        self.server.shutdown()
27	        self.server.server_close()
28	        self.thread.join(timeout=5)
29	        shutil.rmtree(self.tmp, ignore_errors=True)
30	    def request(self, method, path, payload=None):
31	        body = None if payload is None else json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
32	        req = urllib.request.Request(self.base + path, data=body, method=method)
33	        if body is not None:
34	            req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
35	        try:
36	            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as response:
37	                return response.status, json.loads(response.read().decode("utf-8"))
38	        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
39	            return exc.code, json.loads(exc.read().decode("utf-8"))
40	    def write(self, labels, samples, metric="latency_ms", tenant="acme", status=202):

52	        self.assertEqual((first["written"], first["duplicates"]), (3, 0))

"""Tests for obsd.http_app: live ThreadingHTTPServer over a real socket."""

import json
import os
import shutil
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

from obsd import AlertEngine, SeriesStore, create_server


class HttpCase(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="obsd-http-")
        root = os.path.join(self.tmp, "data")
        self.store = SeriesStore(root)
        self.engine = AlertEngine(self.store, root)
        self.server = create_server(self.store, self.engine, "127.0.0.1", 0)
        self.base = "http://127.0.0.1:%d" % self.server.server_address[1]
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()
    def tearDown(self):
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()
        self.thread.join(timeout=5)
        shutil.rmtree(self.tmp, ignore_errors=True)
    def request(self, method, path, payload=None):
        body = None if payload is None else json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
        req = urllib.request.Request(self.base + path, data=body, method=method)
        if body is not None:
            req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as response:
                return response.status, json.loads(response.read().decode("utf-8"))
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            return exc.code, json.loads(exc.read().decode("utf-8"))
    def write(self, labels, samples, metric="latency_ms", tenant="acme", status=202):
        code, body = self.request("POST", "/v1/series", {
            "tenant": tenant, "metric": metric, "labels": labels, "samples": samples})
        self.assertEqual(code, status)
        return body
class TestHttpApi(HttpCase):
    def test_healthz(self):
        code, body = self.request("GET", "/healthz")
        self.assertEqual(code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body, {"ok": True})
    def test_write_then_query_with_step_and_agg(self):
        first = self.write({"host": "a"}, [[0, 1.0], [1000, 3.0], [2000, 5.0]])
        self.assertEqual((first["written"], first["duplicates"]), (3, 0))
        second = self.write({"host": "a"}, [[0, 1.0], [1000, 3.0], [2000, 5.0]])
        self.assertEqual((second["written"], second["duplicates"]), (0, 3))
        code, body = self.request(
            "GET", "/v1/query?tenant=acme&metric=latency_ms&label.host=a&step=1000&agg=avg")
        self.assertEqual(code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["series"][0]["labels"], {"host": "a"})
        self.assertEqual(body["series"][0]["points"], [[0, 1.0], [1000, 3.0], [2000, 5.0]])
    def test_conflicting_write_returns_409(self):
        self.write({}, [[1000, 1.0]])
        code, body = self.request("POST", "/v1/series", {
            "tenant": "acme", "metric": "latency_ms", "labels": {}, "samples": [[1000, 2.0]]})
        self.assertEqual(code, 409)
        self.assertIn("conflict", body["error"])
    def test_malformed_request_returns_400_json_error(self):
        code, body = self.request("POST", "/v1/series", {"metric": "latency_ms"})
        self.assertEqual(code, 400)
        self.assertIn("missing field", body["error"])
        code, body = self.request("GET", "/v1/nope")
        self.assertEqual(code, 404)
        self.assertIn("not found", body["error"])
    def test_rule_evaluate_alerts_and_silence(self):
        self.write({}, [[60000, 5.0], [65000, 5.0]])
        code, rule = self.request("POST", "/v1/rules", {
            "id": "r1", "tenant": "acme", "metric": "latency_ms", "labels": {},
            "comparator": "<", "threshold": 10.0, "for_ms": 0, "window_ms": 30000,
            "agg": "avg", "severity": "warning", "annotations": {"summary": "slow"}})
        self.assertEqual(code, 201)
        self.assertEqual(rule["id"], "r1")
        code, listed = self.request("GET", "/v1/rules?tenant=acme")
        self.assertEqual(code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(len(listed["rules"]), 1)

        code, evaluated = self.request("POST", "/v1/evaluate", {"now_ms": 68000})
        self.assertEqual(code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(len(evaluated["firing"]), 1)
        alert_id = evaluated["firing"][0]["id"]

        # Same condition again: same alert id (dedup), occurrences incremented.
        code, again = self.request("POST", "/v1/evaluate", {"now_ms": 69000})
        self.assertEqual(again["firing"][0]["id"], alert_id)
        self.assertEqual(again["firing"][0]["occurrences"], 2)

        code, alerts = self.request("GET", "/v1/alerts?tenant=acme&state=firing")
        self.assertEqual(code, 200)
        self.assertEqual([row["id"] for row in alerts["alerts"]], [alert_id])

        code, silence = self.request("POST", "/v1/silences", {
            "tenant": "acme", "labels": {}, "starts_ms": 0, "ends_ms": 90000,
            "reason": "maintenance"})
        self.assertEqual(code, 201)
        code, silenced = self.request("POST", "/v1/evaluate", {"now_ms": 70000})
        self.assertEqual(silenced["firing"], [])
        self.assertEqual(len(silenced["silenced"]), 1)
        self.assertEqual(silenced["silenced"][0]["silenced_by"], silence["id"])
    def test_evaluate_without_now_ms_is_rejected(self):
        code, body = self.request("POST", "/v1/evaluate", {})
        self.assertEqual(code, 400)
        self.assertIn("now_ms", body["error"])
    def test_group_by_query_and_errors(self):
        self.write({"host": "a"}, [[0, 1.0], [1000, 3.0]])
        self.write({"host": "b"}, [[1000, 9.0]])
        code, body = self.request(
            "GET", "/v1/query?tenant=acme&metric=latency_ms&agg=avg&group_by=%5B%22host%22%5D")
        self.assertEqual(code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body, {"series": [
            {"labels": {"host": "a"}, "points": [[0, 2.0]]},
            {"labels": {"host": "b"}, "points": [[1000, 9.0]]}]})
        # An empty group_by array merges every matching series into one group.
        code, body = self.request(
            "GET", "/v1/query?tenant=acme&metric=latency_ms&agg=avg&group_by=%5B%5D")
        self.assertEqual(body, {"series": [{"labels": {}, "points": [[0, 13.0 / 3.0]]}]})
        # Malformed group_by values are 400 with the usual error object.
        for group_by in ("[host", "%22host%22", "%5B%22host%22%2C%22host%22%5D", "%5B%5D"):
            code, body = self.request(
                "GET", "/v1/query?tenant=acme&metric=latency_ms&group_by=" + group_by)
            self.assertEqual(code, 400, group_by)
            self.assertIn("error", body)
        code, body = self.request(
            "GET", "/v1/query?tenant=acme&metric=latency_ms&agg=median&group_by=%5B%5D")
        self.assertEqual(code, 400)
        self.assertIn("error", body)
    def test_quotas_set_get_usage_and_enforcement(self):
        code, body = self.request("GET", "/v1/quotas?tenant=acme")
        self.assertEqual(code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body, {"tenant": "acme", "max_series": None, "max_points": None,
                                "series": 0, "points": 0})
        code, body = self.request("POST", "/v1/quotas",
                                  {"tenant": "acme", "max_series": 1, "max_points": 2})
        self.assertEqual(code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body, {"tenant": "acme", "max_series": 1, "max_points": 2,
                                "series": 0, "points": 0})
        self.write({}, [[1000, 1.0], [2000, 2.0]])
        code, body = self.request("GET", "/v1/quotas?tenant=acme")
        self.assertEqual((code, body["series"], body["points"]), (200, 1, 2))
        # A batch exceeding max_points is rejected with 409 and changes nothing.
        code, body = self.request("POST", "/v1/series", {
            "tenant": "acme", "metric": "latency_ms", "labels": {},
            "samples": [[2000, 2.0], [3000, 3.0]]})
        self.assertEqual(code, 409)
        self.assertIn("quota exceeded", body["error"])
        code, body = self.request("GET", "/v1/quotas?tenant=acme")
        self.assertEqual((body["series"], body["points"]), (1, 2))
        # Duplicates and overwrites still succeed at the limit.
        self.write({}, [[1000, 1.0]])
        code, body = self.request("POST", "/v1/series", {
            "tenant": "acme", "metric": "latency_ms", "labels": {},
            "samples": [[1000, 9.0]], "overwrite": True})
        self.assertEqual(code, 202)
        # A second series hits max_series with 409.
        code, body = self.request("POST", "/v1/series", {
            "tenant": "acme", "metric": "latency_ms", "labels": {"host": "b"},
            "samples": [[1000, 1.0]]})
        self.assertEqual(code, 409)
        self.assertIn("max_series", body["error"])
    def test_invalid_quota_requests_return_400_and_keep_config(self):
        self.request("POST", "/v1/quotas", {"tenant": "acme", "max_series": 1, "max_points": 4})
        for bad in (True, "1", 1.5, -1):
            code, body = self.request("POST", "/v1/quotas",
                                      {"tenant": "acme", "max_series": bad, "max_points": 4})
            self.assertEqual(code, 400, repr(bad))
            self.assertIn("error", body)
        code, body = self.request("POST", "/v1/quotas",
                                  {"tenant": "", "max_series": 1, "max_points": 1})
        self.assertEqual(code, 400)
        code, body = self.request("GET", "/v1/quotas")
        self.assertEqual(code, 400)
        code, body = self.request("GET", "/v1/quotas?tenant=acme")
        self.assertEqual((code, body["max_series"], body["max_points"]), (200, 1, 4))
    def test_slo_set_and_status(self):
        self.write({}, [[index * 1000, 1.0 if index else 0.0] for index in range(10)])
        code, slo = self.request("POST", "/v1/slos", {
            "tenant": "acme", "name": "availability", "metric": "latency_ms", "labels": {},
            "good_comparator": ">=", "threshold": 1.0, "target_ratio": 0.9, "window_ms": 60000})
        self.assertEqual(code, 201)
        self.assertEqual(slo["name"], "availability")
        code, status = self.request(
            "GET", "/v1/slos/status?tenant=acme&name=availability&now_ms=60000")
        self.assertEqual(code, 200)
        self.assertEqual((status["total"], status["good"], status["bad"]), (10, 9, 1))
        self.assertAlmostEqual(status["ratio"], 0.9)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(status["error_budget"], 0.0)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(status["burn_rate"], 1.0)
        self.assertTrue(status["met"])
if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
